CruiseMapper currently has no ship schedule for Port Addu Atoll Maldives (Gan Island)

Addu Atoll (port locode MVADU), fka Seenu Atoll, is the Maldives' southernmost atoll, located approx 541 km (336 ml) south of Male (Kaafu Atoll). In this atoll is located Addu City, one of the country's only two cities (together with Male).

Addu City comprises of all Addu Atoll's inhabited areas, which are on the islands Feydhoo, Hithadhoo, Hulhudhoo, Maradhoo, and Meedhoo, plus several uninhabited islands, among which is Gan Island, where the atoll's only airport (Gan International Airport) is located.

Addu Atoll features a natural anchorage, as its waters are protected by large islands surrounding it. The result is a natural, calm and safe at all times harbor waterway, not affected by seasonal climate changes. The atoll has 4 channels, all leading into its lagoon.

Barrier reefs protect the atoll's islands from the Indian Ocean's storms and high waves. This allows coconut palms to grow everywhere on the isles. The islands also feature small lakes, wetlands, marshy fields and white terns (small tropical seabirds) which in the Maldives can be found only in this atoll. The fauna is also represented by whales and dolphins, with a great variety of species.

Atoll's inhabited islands are named (alphabetically listed) Feydhoo, Hithadhoo, Hulhudhoo, Maradhoo, and Meedhoo. These islands also form Addu City's 5 districts. All these islands are natural and well-connected.

Atoll's uninhabited islands are named (alphabetically listed):

  • Aboohéra
  • Bodu Hajara, Boduheragandu
  • Dhigihera
  • Fahikedeherangada
  • Gan Island (Gan International Airport), Gaukendi, Geskalhuhera
  • Hankede, Hankede, Hajara, Hera, Here-there (Herathera Island Resort), Hikahera
  • Kafathalhaa, Kandu Huraa, Kedevaahera Koahera Kuda, Kandihereganda
  • Maahera, Maamendhoo, Madihera, Mulikede
  • Savaaheli
  • Vashahéra, Villingili (Shangri-La Resort)

Addu Atoll Maldives cruise terminal

Most cruise ships to Addu Atoll dock (anchor) at Gan Island, where is located the Gan International Airport.

At a Glance

Independent sightseeing: Independent with some planning or transport. Cruise ships calling at Addu Atoll normally anchor near Gan Island rather than berth at a conve:contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}efore go ashore by tender or local boat, with the exact landing point arranged for the individual call.

Gan itself is suitable for a short independent visit, particularly for its former British military sites. For the more interesting wetlands, local communities and scenery of the western islands, a taxi or pre-arranged vehicle is much more practical. Gan, Feydhoo, Maradhoo-Feydhoo, Maradhoo and Hithadhoo are connected by road.

Getting from the Cruise Port

There is no conventional walk-off cruise terminal. Most large cruise ships remain at anchor near Gan, so allow additional time for tendering in both directions and confirm the day's landing point and last-tender arrangements on board.

Once ashore on Gan, taxis or arranged vehicles are the most useful transport for a cruise visit. The road connection continues through the neighboring islands to Hithadhoo. Gan International Airport to central Hithadhoo is roughly 13 km (8.1 mi) by road, while the full road corridor between Gan and the northern part of Hithadhoo is about 16 km (9.9 mi).

Local buses operate on the connected islands, but cruise passengers should not depend on an unfamiliar timetable for the return journey. A taxi or pre-arranged driver provides substantially more control over the day.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Gan and the Former RAF Base

Allow 1.5–2.5 hours. Easy independently if the tender lands on Gan.

Gan was used as a British military base, and surviving reminders include the Addu Atoll Memorial, former RAF buildings and other remnants around the old base area. Equator Village occupies part of the former military complex. The airport runway itself also developed from the former airfield.

This is the simplest choice for passengers who do not want a long transfer. Most sightseeing is on level terrain, although shade can be limited and the tropical heat makes even modest walks tiring.

Drive the Connected Islands to Hithadhoo

Allow about 2.5–4 hours. Practical independently with a taxi or arranged vehicle.

A drive from Gan through Feydhoo and Maradhoo to Hithadhoo is one of the best ways to see how Addu differs from a resort island. The causeways and coastal road pass local neighborhoods, mosques, small shops, cafés and stretches of lagoon shoreline.

Rather than treating Hithadhoo as a single major attraction, use the journey as a scenic local-island tour and combine it with Addu Nature Park. Agree with the driver on waiting time and the return to the tender point before setting out.

Addu Nature Park

Allow 2.5–3.5 hours including transport from Gan. Independent with pre-arranged transport.

At the northern end of Hithadhoo, Addu Nature Park protects the Eydhigali Kilhi wetlands and Koattey area. Visitors can see mangroves, freshwater wetlands, birdlife and coastal vegetation from roads, paths and viewing structures. White terns are a characteristic sight in Addu.

The park is around a 20–30 minute drive from the Gan area under normal conditions. Walking, cycling, buggy rides and canoeing have been offered within the park, but activity availability should be confirmed locally rather than assumed for a cruise call.

Diving and Lagoon Trips

Allow at least 3–4 hours. Organized excursion recommended.

Addu is particularly strong for scuba diving, with reefs, manta encounters and the British Loyalty wreck among its best-known underwater attractions. The wreck is reached by boat and is a scuba-diving site rather than a casual shore-snorkeling stop.

For a cruise call, use a ship excursion or an established local dive operator that understands the ship's departure time. Boat transfers, equipment preparation and sea conditions make this a poor activity to improvise after arriving ashore.

Self-Guided Walking Tour: Gan RAF Heritage

Difficulty: Easy. Mostly flat, but hot and humid with limited shade in places.

Distance: Approximately 3–4 km (1.9–2.5 mi), depending on the day's tender landing point and accessible lanes. Allow 40–60 minutes of actual walking and about 1.5–2 hours with stops.

  1. Gan tender landing area: Confirm the exact return point and last tender before leaving.
  2. Former RAF district: Walk through the area associated with the former British air base and look for surviving military-era structures.
  3. Addu Atoll Memorial: Visit the memorial near the former RAF headquarters, commemorating servicemen who died while stationed in Addu.
  4. Former military buildings: Continue past surviving remnants such as the old cinema and other base structures where accessible.
  5. Equator Village area: The resort incorporates former RAF mess buildings. Do not assume access to hotel facilities unless permission or a day arrangement has been confirmed.
  6. Lagoon-side return: Use the quieter coastal lanes where practical before returning directly to the tender point.

This route is preferable to attempting to walk toward Feydhoo or Hithadhoo. The linked islands are better explored by vehicle or bicycle because the complete road corridor extends around 16 km (9.9 mi).

Beaches and Nature

Addu has attractive lagoon and ocean shorelines, but not every stretch of coast is a managed swimming beach. Reef, currents and access conditions vary, and entry to resort beaches should not be assumed. Passengers mainly interested in swimming or snorkeling are better served by a confirmed local boat trip, dive/snorkel operator or ship-arranged beach activity.

When an Organized Excursion Makes More Sense

Choose an organized or pre-arranged excursion for scuba diving, snorkeling by boat, manta or dolphin trips, visits to islands not connected to Gan by road, or any itinerary involving multiple boat transfers. Meedhoo and Hulhudhoo lie separately on the eastern side of the atoll and require a boat connection, making them less suitable for an improvised independent visit during a short call.

Practical Tips

  • Tendering can consume a significant part of the port call, especially when many passengers go ashore at once.
  • For travel beyond Gan, arrange the return vehicle before starting sightseeing rather than relying on finding transport later.
  • Dress modestly when visiting the inhabited islands of Feydhoo, Maradhoo and Hithadhoo. Resort rules differ from local-island customs.
  • Sun protection and drinking water are important; heat and humidity can make walking more demanding than the distances suggest.
  • Allow a generous return margin. For independent trips, aim to be back at the tender landing area well before the ship's stated last tender, particularly after visiting Hithadhoo or taking a boat excursion.
